title: Arshad Warsi Just Walked Back Into the Hirani-Verse — and He Brought Everyone
excerpt: Rajkumar Hirani's first-ever series premieres Thursday on JioHotstar. His son is the lead. Vikrant Massey is the villain. And Sanjay Dutt apparently couldn't stay away.
body:
The man who gave us Munna Bhai, 3 Idiots, and PK — arguably the most perfect commercial filmmaker India has ever produced — has never made a television series. Not once. In a streaming landscape drowning in derivative crime thrillers and lifeless franchise extensions, Rajkumar Hirani simply stayed away. Until now.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=uCjkRVV0-qU

Pritam and Pedro, his first-ever series, premieres this Thursday, July 3, on JioHotstar. And if the trailer is any indication, the Hirani-verse doesn't shrink on a smaller screen. It just gets weirder.

Goa, Hackers, and a Severed Finger

Set against the sun-drenched chaos of Goa, the series follows Pedro (Arshad Warsi), a gut-instinct cop who trusts his *danda* more than any database, and Pritam (Vir Hirani), a tech-savvy young investigator who speaks in algorithms. Together, they're thrown into a kidnapping case involving a politician's son, a ransom in the millions, and a cybercriminal who makes your blood run cold.

That criminal is Martin, played by Vikrant Massey — and if you know Massey only as the tender-eyed sweetheart of *12th Fail*, prepare to meet someone else entirely. In the trailer, Martin cuts off a child's middle finger as a threat. Then he laughs. It's the kind of moment that makes you pause, rewind, and wonder what happened to the man who once made you cry over a civil services exam.

> "I was sick of playing *gaav ka gareeb* or a boy-next-door. Finally, sir gave me an opportunity." — Vikrant Massey

Massey, who won a National Award for Best Actor for his luminous turn in *12th Fail*, has been quietly sharpening his edge since *Sector 36*. In Martin, he's found something genuinely unsettling — an antagonist who, in true Hirani fashion, isn't a cardboard villain but a character with texture, subtext, and a reason you'll almost understand.

The Son Who Walked Into His Father's Office

The most compelling casting story, though, belongs to Vir Hirani — Rajkumar's son, making his screen debut as Pritam. The elder Hirani has been almost disarmingly transparent about how it happened: Vir was studying in London when the casting process began. Nobody was considering him. Then he came home, walked into his father's production office, and told the team: *"You're looking for an actor — there's one sitting at home."*

What followed wasn't a shortcut. Avinash Arun, the director of *Paatal Lok* and *Three of Us*, went to see Vir perform in Feroz Abbas Khan's stage production *Letters of Suresh*. Then Vir shot 40 to 50 audition scenes before Arun told Hirani: we should take him.

At the trailer launch, Arshad — who has never met a moment he couldn't turn into a bit — captured the dynamic perfectly. Vir had a habit of standing in a slouch. Rajkumar would tell him, *"Beta, seedhe khade raho."* Vir would shrug it off. Then Arshad said the same thing, and Vir immediately straightened up: *"Yes, sir."*

Arshad's punchline brought the house down: *"Baap ki koi izzat nahin hoti hai, chahe aapka baap Rajkumar Hirani kyun na ho!"*

Circuit, Pedro, and the Reunion That Matters

For Warsi, this is his third collaboration with Hirani after the two *Munna Bhai* films — a partnership that gave Hindi cinema one of its most beloved characters in Circuit. As Pedro, the sun-weathered Goa cop suspicious of anything that runs on Wi-Fi, he brings a completely different energy: grizzled, territorial, magnificently analogue.

> "I think Raju has a little faith in me as an actor. He gives me various things to do. And I like it." — Arshad Warsi

The supporting cast is stacked. Boman Irani and Mona Singh hold pivotal roles. Shantanu Moitra composes the music. Swanand Kirkire writes the lyrics. And in what was supposed to be a closely guarded secret — until Arshad cheerfully blurted it out at the trailer launch — Sanjay Dutt makes an appearance. Because of course Munna couldn't let Circuit go to Goa alone.

Shreya Ghoshal added her own flourish at the event, performing the track *'Piya Piya Piya'* live and sending the room into a frenzy.

Where to Watch

The series is being described as "a world where data meets *danda*, chaos meets confusion" — and with a real cybersecurity expert, Amit Dubey, serving as consultant (he hacked a journalist's phone live at the trailer launch, just to make a point), the tech side isn't window dressing.

Pritam and Pedro streams exclusively on JioHotstar from July 3 — available across India, the US, UK, Canada, and most international markets. For diaspora viewers who've been waiting for a series that carries Hirani's signature warmth and mischief without the bloat, this is the one to clear your Thursday evening for.

The Hirani-verse has entered streaming. And knowing this man's track record — zero misfires across two decades — it might already be the most dangerous thing on any platform.
